key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskite nanoflakes.
Assessed environmental light and thermal stability.
Probed degradation using confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative lifetime or solar-cell efficiency results and describes materials characterization, not AI-based research.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
